standard_prerequisites.name: The representation of the solutions of the limiting equation by hypergeometric functions
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: same article, the representation introduced in the preceding section
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the limit of the difference of the two solutions at infinity by evaluating the hypergeometric function at zero.

standard_prerequisites.name: The explicit equation satisfied by the difference of the two solutions
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the problem into a forced harmonic oscillator equation whose solution is written by the variation of constants formula.

standard_prerequisites.name: The uniform bound for the comparison solution
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: same article, the lemma at source lines 237-244
standard_prerequisites.use: Bounds the forcing term and hence the integral that appears in the variation of constants formula.

core_obligations: Show that the differences of the two solutions and of their derivatives vanish at infinity by evaluating the hypergeometric representation at the origin (proof lines 329-336).
Derive the inhomogeneous equation satisfied by the difference, with the forcing term given by the deviation of the squared hyperbolic tangent from one times the solution (proof lines 337-338).
Write the difference by the variation of constants formula with initial data at a finite point and pass to the limit in the initial point (proof lines 339-342).

Bound the remaining integral by the forcing term through the uniform bound for the comparison solution and integrate the difference against the decay of the deviation, first for the solution and then for the derivative (proof lines 343-346).
proof_roadmap: Vanishing of the differences at infinity (proof lines 329-336).
Inhomogeneous equation for the difference (proof lines 337-338).
Variation of constants and the bound on the integral (proof lines 339-346).
